Kirjath-sepher
KIR-jath-SEE-fur
proper noun
Hebrew Qiryath-sepher, “city of the book” or “town of the scribe,” the older name of Debir in the hill country of Judah.

Biblical Definition

Kirjath-sepher, “the city of the book,” was the former name of Debir, a town in the hill country of Judah (Josh 15:15). When Caleb came to drive out the sons of Anak and take possession of his inheritance, he made a promise: “He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife” (Josh 15:16). Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took the city, and won Achsah for his bride; and the same Othniel afterward became the first of the judges, on whom the Spirit of the LORD came to deliver Israel (Judg 3:9–10). Achsah, asking her father for a field, prayed also for springs of water, and Caleb gave her the upper and the nether springs (Josh 15:19). The town was later given to the priests as one of their cities (Josh 21:15). The name “city of the book” has stirred much wonder, suggesting a place of writing or record among the Canaanites. Whatever learning the old city held, it could not save it from the hand of the LORD’s people; and the man who took it rose to be the first deliverer of Israel. Kirjath-sepher witnesses that valour rewarded in faith opens the way to greater service in the kingdom of God.

Webster 1828 Definition

The old name of Debir, “city of the book,” taken by Othniel, who won Caleb’s daughter and became Israel’s first judge.

KIRJATH-SEPHER, the former name of Debir, a town in the hill country of Judah.

Its name signifies “city of the book” or “town of the scribe.”

Caleb offered his daughter Achsah to whoever should take it (Josh 15:16).

Othniel took the city and won Achsah to wife (Josh 15:17).

Othniel afterward became the first of the judges of Israel (Judg 3:9).

Key Scripture

Josh 15:15 — "And he went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjathsepher."

Josh 15:16 — "And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjathsepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife."

Josh 15:17 — "And Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife."

Judg 1:13 — "And Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife."

Modern Corruption

A place-name, not a doctrine in dispute; its lesson is that valour exercised in faith opens the way to greater service.

expand to see more

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is the path from Kirjath-sepher to the seat of the judge. Othniel proved himself in the taking of the city, and the man who was faithful in that smaller charge was raised up by the Spirit of God to deliver all Israel. The Lord trains His servants for great work by their faithfulness in lesser tasks.

The “city of the book,” whatever its learning, fell before the people of God; and it is worth remembering that the only book that abides is the book of the LORD. The records and wisdom of the nations pass away with their cities, but the word of our God shall stand for ever. Achsah’s request for the springs of water also teaches the boldness of faith that asks for the fuller blessing and is not denied.

Hebrew Roots

The name joins qiryah, “city,” with sepher, “book” or “writing,” hence “city of the book.”

expand to see more

Kirjath-sepher — Hebrew Qiryath-sepher, “city of the book.”

The element qiryah means city or town.

Sepher denotes a book, scroll, or writing.

It was the older name of the town later called Debir.

The city of the book was taken by the future first judge of Israel.

Usage

"Like Othniel at Kirjath-sepher, the servant faithful in a smaller charge is raised to a greater."

"Kirjath-sepher teaches that the books and learning of the nations pass away, but the word of God abides."

"Achsah’s prayer for the springs shows the faith that asks the fuller blessing and is heard."
